subproblem.title: Hadamard's inequality for Gram determinants: det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) ≤ ∏|v_i|²
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let v = (v_1, …, v_n) (indexed by Fin n) be an arbitrary family of vectors in ℝ^P (Euclid P); no independence is assumed. Then the Gram determinant satisfies det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} ≤ ∏_{i=1}^n |v_i|². Here ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm, and the determinant is that of the n×n real matrix with entries ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)). For n = 0 both sides equal 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Euclid P), Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)) ≤ ∏ i, ‖v i‖ ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (Hadamard: Γ(v) ≤ Π_j |v_j|², the dependent case by a kernel vector of the Gram matrix and the independent case by Gram–Schmidt), with the details filled in. The Gram–Schmidt part is the sibling gs_frame (the comparator-accepted declaration dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram). This is the classical Hadamard inequality for Gram determinants.
Notation: ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm of ℝ^P. G is the n×n real matrix G_{ij} := ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)), and Γ(v) := det G. Since |v_i|² ≥ 0 for every i, the right-hand side ∏_i |v_i|² is ≥ 0 (Finset.prod_nonneg, sq_nonneg).
1. Case split. Either v is linearly independent over ℝ (steps 5–6) or it is not (steps 2–4).
2. Dependent case: a nonzero coefficient vector. If v is linearly dependent, there is c = (c_1, …, c_n) ∈ ℝ^n with Σ_j c_j v_j = 0 and c_{i₀} ≠ 0 for some index i₀ (Fintype.not_linearIndependent_iff). In particular c ≠ 0. (In the parent's notation, Vc = 0, where V is the P×n matrix with columns v_j.)
3. Dependent case: Gc = 0. For each i, (Gc)_i = Σ_j ⟨v_i, v_j⟩c_j = Σ_j ⟨v_i, c_j v_j⟩ = ⟨v_i, Σ_j c_j v_j⟩ = ⟨v_i, 0⟩ = 0. This uses linearity of the inner product in its second argument (real_inner_smul_right, inner_sum, inner_zero_right). So G = VᵀV maps the nonzero vector c to 0.
4. Dependent case: conclusion. A square real matrix that sends a nonzero vector to 0 has determinant 0 (Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff: (∃ c ≠ 0, G *ᵥ c = 0) ↔ det G = 0). Hence Γ(v) = 0 ≤ ∏_i |v_i|².
5. Independent case: Gram–Schmidt. If v is linearly independent, apply the sibling gs_frame to v. It gives an orthonormal family σ = (σ_1, …, σ_n), the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization of v, with the following property. Let A be the n×n matrix A_{ij} := ⟨σ_i, v_j⟩ (the upper-triangular matrix T of the parent's step 4). Then (i) Γ(v) = (det A)² and (iii) |det A| ≤ ∏_i |v_i|.
6. Independent case: conclusion. 0 ≤ |det A| ≤ ∏_i |v_i|, and t ↦ t² is monotone on [0, ∞) (pow_le_pow_left₀). So Γ(v) = (det A)² = |det A|² ≤ (∏_i |v_i|)² = ∏_i |v_i|² (sq_abs, Finset.prod_pow).
7. Edge cases need no separate treatment. For n = 0 the empty family is linearly independent, and steps 5–6 give Γ(v) = det(empty matrix) = 1 ≤ 1 = the empty product. A family with some v_i = 0, e.g. P = 0 with n ≥ 1, is linearly dependent and falls under steps 2–4. ∎
Formalization notes (checked: this proof compiles after import GMT.Ch07.Submission in the comparator's contract scope, with the gs_frame statement as a hypothesis; #print axioms gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]). intro P n v; by_cases hv : LinearIndependent ℝ v.
- Independent: obtain ⟨σ, -, -, hG, -, hA⟩ := Submission.dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram P n v hv; rw [hG, Finset.prod_pow, ← sq_abs]; exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (abs_nonneg _) hA 2.
- Dependent: obtain ⟨c, hc, i₀, hi₀⟩ := Fintype.not_linearIndependent_iff.mp hv. Prove the determinant is zero by rw [← Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff] with the witness ⟨c, fun h => hi₀ (congrFun h i₀), _⟩ and funext i. Then simp only [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Matrix.of_apply, Pi.zero_apply]. Show Σ_j inner ℝ (v i) (v j) * c j = inner ℝ (v i) (Σ_j c j • v j) by rw [inner_sum], then Finset.sum_congr with real_inner_smul_right and mul_comm, and finish with rw [this, hc, inner_zero_right]. Then rw [hdet]; exact Finset.prod_nonneg fun i _ => sq_nonneg _.
- Mathlib's Matrix.gram and LinearMap.normDet are not imported by the contract and are not needed.
proof_key_steps: Split on whether v is linearly independent.
Dependent: Σ_j c_j v_j = 0 with c ≠ 0 gives (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)·c = 0, so Γ(v) = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) = 0 ≤ ∏|v_i|².
Independent: the sibling gs_frame gives A = (⟨σ_i, v_j⟩) with Γ(v) = (det A)² and |det A| ≤ ∏|v_i|.
Square the nonnegative bound: Γ(v) = |det A|² ≤ (∏|v_i|)² = ∏|v_i|².
